item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. SCOPe treats these proteins as a fold-level structural convergence or remote structural grouping, not as one demonstrated homologous superfamily. They are in the membrane-protein class and share the heme-binding four-helical-bundle fold, corresponding to the SCOP/SCOPe hierarchy f.21, but the named groups are split at superfamily level: transmembrane di-heme cytochromes are f.21.1, fumarate-reductase respiratory-complex transmembrane subunits are f.21.2, and respiratory nitrate-reductase gamma chains are f.21.3. That means the shared four-helix, two-heme transmembrane architecture is evidence for the same fold only. SCOPe does not assert a common ancestor for f.21.1, f.21.2, and f.21.3, so it would be unsafe to merge them into one homologous superfamily, to pick representatives as if they were redundant homologs, or to transfer detailed function, chain topology, or residue-level heme-ligation annotations across the three groups on SCOPe classification alone. A structure from one of the three can at most be used as an analogy or fold template for the other two unless independent sequence, phylogenetic, or comparative structural evidence establishes homology for the particular proteins being compared.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
